question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Raining cats and dogs

options.text: something that does not upset you

solution:
The correct answer is **"it is raining very heavily."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"raining cats and dogs"** means heavy rain. (भारी वर्षा)

 
 
• **Example:*** Don't forget to take your umbrella - it's **raining cats and dogs**__ out there.*
 
 
 
• The idiom is often used in informal conversations and writing to describe a particularly heavy rainstorm.
 
• Other similar idioms include** "pouring rain"** and **"bucketing down."**

**Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.**
